Commentary.Commentary: The clouds have started to steadily hover in over the ground. It's a bit windy out there and couple that with a green track, a difficult task lies ahead for the Zimbabweans. Against the swinging ball, it'll be a test of their character and they're going to have to really apply themselves. The rain could come in to affect how this game goes as well so it remains to be seen how it plays out. Join us in a short while for the run chase.

Zimbabwe will be a little disappointed with themselves. They bowled well throughout but could not keep a lid on things very well at the death. Leaked a few more runs than they would have liked. Tendai Chatara took 3 wickets in the final 5 overs, 2 of which came in the final over. Graeme Cremer was the pick of the bowlers though, he came on to bowl at a crucial time and kept things in check, even picked up two crucial wickets, of Shahzad and Stanikzai.

Wickets kept falling at regular intervals and Zimbabwe were getting on top, but a solid yet brisk 45-run partnership between Mohammad Nabi and Najibullah Zadran brought things back on track. The latter continued on after the former's departure and scored some vital blows towards the end of the innings. It helped his side post a good total on the board.

Afghanistan will be pleased overall with the score they've managed to put on the board. After electing to bat, they lost Noor Ali Zadran relatively early but then Mohammad Shahzad and Rahmat Shah did well to play against the swinging ball. They stuck in and built a good partnership of 84 runs. Both departed shortly after but completed their respective fifties before doing so.
OUT c Graeme Cremer b Tendai Chatara. Afghanistan have lost their ninth wicket.
OUT Dawlat Zadran run out (Peter Moor). Afghanistan have lost their eighth wicket.
OUT b Tendai Chatara. Afghanistan have lost their seventh wicket.
OUT c Tarisai Musakanda b Chris Mpofu. Afghanistan have lost their sixth wicket.

After 45 overs, Afghanistan have crossed the 200-run mark, stay on 201 for the loss of 5 wickets. After being hit for runs at a brisk pace, Zimbabwe have clawed back with a wicket via Richard Ngarava. The pacer pounded in another short one, much like his wicket-taking delivery against Noor Ali Zadran, and got Mohammad Nabi to nick it behind on his attempted pull shot. A big wicket for the hosts, can they now pick up wickets in succession and restrict the Afghans to a decent score?
OUT c Peter Moor b Richard Ngarava. Afghanistan have lost their fifth wicket.

After 40 overs, Afghanistan lie at 182/4. The current pair of Mohammad Nabi and Najibullah Zadran is motoring along with the former taking most of the attack to the opposition bowlers. He is making most of the life given to him by Graeme Cremer and looks set to make Zimbabwe pay. A lot rides on these two batsmen, could be the defining factor of the match. Zimbabwe need to find a way to get a wicket somehow, otherwise they could run the risk of letting it slip out of their hands.

After 35 overs, Afghanistan are struggling at 149/4. Zimbabwe are right on top of this game now as Graeme Cremer struck once again. He took out out his counterpart by getting him caught at long off by Musakanda. Huge blow in itself which was followed by another quick wicket. Tendai Chatara caught Rahmat Shah leg before and the Afghanistan no.3 batsman departed after scoring a half century. The home side is in control of things right now and the Afghans are in a real spot of bother now. Need something special from the lower middle order.
OUT lbw b Tendai Chatara. Afghanistan have lost their fourth wicket.
OUT c Tarisai Musakanda b Graeme Cremer. Afghanistan have lost their third wicket.

After 30 overs, Afghanistan are moving slowly but have lost a vital wicket, are 128/2 now. Success for the hosts as the Zimbabwean skipper Graeme Cremer scalped the all-important wicket of Mohammad Shahzad, completely against the run of play, by bowling him out 'round his legs. Breaking the partnership of 84 runs, he has given his team a much-needed breakthrough and a chance to make further inroads. The visiting team needs to be careful here, a quick wicket or two at this point could see them in some trouble. Important period of play coming up for both teams.
OUT b Graeme Cremer. Afghanistan have lost their second wicket.

Halfway through the first innings and after 25 overs, Afghanistan move along to 107/1. The runs are cautiously coming as both batsmen are finding the odd boundary here and there. Mohammad Shahzad has notched up a gritty fifty, he's had to curb his natural game and has done well to adjust to the conditions so far. The Zimbabwe bowlers are maintaining a tight line and not leaking many runs, but they need to break this partnership, which is building nicely right now.

After 20 overs, Afghanistan have not lost another wicket and are 84/1. The current pair of Mohammad Shahzad and Rahmat Shah have slowly grown into the game after steadying things a bit. The Zimbabweans may have slightly lost some concentration which has led to their lines wavering a bit. Big moment in the match on the final ball of the 17th over, the dangerous Shahzad was dropped out in the deep by Musakanda as the batsman tried to clear the cover boundary. Remains to be seen how costly that could prove. The wicket is slowly easing up and things are getting back on somewhat even terms.

After 15 overs, Afghanistan have added 21 runs as they are 55/1 at this stage. The hosts are keeping the pressure on. Excellent lines and good lengths from the bowlers are making the opposition batsmen really work for every run. After losing the early wicket, Mohammad Shahzad and Rahmat Shah have the difficult task of keeping a hold of things and make the scoreboard tick at the same time.

After 10 overs, Afghanistan have lost a wicket and now stand at 34/1. Richard Ngarava struck on the last ball of the first Powerplay with the short ball. Banged it in hard and got Noor Ali Zadran to glove it behind to Peter Moor. Zimbabwe have used the overcast conditions well and bowled smartly. They've kept the pressure on with some good lines and managed to scalp a wicket to break the opening stand.
OUT c Peter Moor b Richard Ngarava. Afghanistan have lost their first wicket.

After 5 overs, Afghanistan are 15/0. They've started steadily and are being as cautious as they can in hitting their shots. Although, Noor Ali Zadran was given an early reprieve as Tendai Chatara dropped him off his own bowling. The Zimbabwe bowlers, despite that, have done well to use the green pitch and restrict the Afghanistan openers from finding the boundary much.

The players and the umpires have made their way out in the middle. Mohammad Shahzad and Noor Ali Zadran will open the innings for the away side. Tendai Chatara will take the new ball first up for Zimbabwe. Unfortunately, due to lack of television feed, there won't be ball-by-ball commentary for this match but we shall keep you posted with updates.

Toss - Afghanistan win the toss and elect to bat first! So it is confirmed, Sikandar Raza is injured and so, Hamilton Masakadza makes his way into the side for him. Just the one change for them. Afghanistan remain unchanged.

Some bit of bad news however, is that the conditions are overcast in Harare. No sign of rain as of now, but showers are forecast as the day progresses. Zimbabwe especially, won't want another one influenced by the showers. Nothing is confirmed yet, but rumours are circling around Sikandar Raza injured himself during practice yesterday. Not sure about his fitness yet, so it remains to be seen whether he will participate today. The home side will have its fingers crossed.

Afghanistan on the other hand, will look to get another win under their belt. They have the momentum on their side and will want to carry it forward. Their skipper is in good form as he led from the front in the first match with a fluent half century. We hope we're in for a good encounter.

Hello and a warm welcome for the 2nd ODI between Zimbabwe and Afghanistan at the Harare Sports Club. The last time 'round, we saw the visitors clinch a victory in a rain-hit series opener. It was pretty unfortunate for the hosts as they were just ahead on DLS Method, but the wicket of Ryan Burl tipped the scales in their opposition's favour. Graeme Cremer and his men will look to tighten the screws and iron out the mistakes from the last game.
